title: Rollout lifecycle ticker and KPI microscope
summary: Compact operational ledger that combines a daily ticker for rollout progress with a focused KPI microscope for early signal detection. Designed for short rhythmic ops checks during phased launches (0-100% traffic) and for rapid decisioning on hold/continue/rollback paths.
purpose: Create a single-pane-of-glass lightweight doc the product-ops rotation can carry during launch windows. It pairs a tiny time-series ticker with ownerable acceptance gates and a short contingency ladder tied to measurable KPI thresholds.
audience: Product ops leads, release engineers, SRE on-call, solutions engineers assigned to the pilot cohort, and the launch commander.
scope: Applies to staged feature rollouts (phased traffic), beta cohort experiments, and incremental capacity ramps for model-serving endpoints. Not intended for infra-only emergency incidents (use SRE runbook).
runway_kpis:
Primary KPIs (observed every 15m during ramp windows):
- P95 latency (api generation) — target < 450ms for small payloads
- Error rate (5xx + client timeouts) — target < 0.5%
- Tokens/sec per host (throughput) — baseline and delta vs. yesterday
- Cost per 1k tokens (observed burn) — alert if > +30% vs. expected
- Quality regression signal (eval set mismatches) — pass/fail; >=1% high-severity tokens flagged triggers triage
Secondary KPIs: CPU/GPU UTIL avg, KV cache hit ratio, queue length, median cold-start time.
ticker_format:
Each ticker row (one line per 15m window during ramp):
- window_start_iso | traffic_pct | p95_ms | errors_pct | tokens_sec | cost_delta_pct | owner | note
Example: 2025-02-20T14:00Z | 10% | 362 | 0.3% | 18.2 | +8% | OmarK | minor batching variance
Use ticker to detect sustained trend (3 consecutive windows) before escalating.
phased_capacity_plan:
Phase 0 (Canary): 0.5% traffic, run 60m, sanity smoke only.
Phase 1: 5% traffic, run 2h, validate latency & error targets.
Phase 2: 25% traffic, run 4h, validate sustained throughput & cost.
Phase 3: 60% traffic, run 8h, monitor cascading effects across regions.
Phase 4: 100% traffic (gradual), continuous monitoring and post-mortem window.
Autoscaling knobs: max-inflight-per-host, batch-size-cap, kv-cache-ttl adjustments. Pre-deploy checks: canary image digest pinned, migration flags off, observability hooks active.
readiness_checklist:
Pre-launch quick checklist (ownerable):
- [ ] Canary image built & digest pinned (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Smoke tests passing on staging with production-like payloads (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Dashboard widgets created for run-window (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Alerting thresholds deployed to PagerDuty (owner: SRE lead)
- [ ] Rollback image and DB migration rollback plan documented (owner: Omar)
- [ ] Contract tests for model output schema & eval set run (owner: Solutions Eng)
- [ ] Security review for downstream customer data flow (owner: Security)
- [ ] Capacity reservation (Dedicated pools) confirmed if needed (owner: infra)
acceptance_criteria:
Gate to move from phase to phase (require all true):
1) P95 latency within target for last 3 windows and trending stable
2) Error rate < threshold for last 3 windows
3) No quality regression alerts on curated eval set
4) Infra metrics (GPU mem pressure, queue length) within safe ranges
5) No open Sev2+ tickets related to this rollout
If any criterion fails, pause and execute contingency ladder.
contingency_triggers:
Immediate triggers and actions: 
- Trigger A (Error spike > 1% sustained 2 windows): throttle traffic by 50% and open triage.
- Trigger B (P95 > target + 2x for 2 windows): rollback to previous model variant.
- Trigger C (Cost burn > +50% expected in 1h): pause further phases, notify finance lead and evaluate quantization flags.
- Trigger D (Quality regression flagged by eval harness): pause and block promotion until root cause review complete.

R (Responsible): Launch Commander (Maya Chen)
A (Accountable): Head of Product Ops
C (Consulted): SRE, Solutions Eng, Infra

raw_notes:
- Keep the ticker intentionally minimal — humans read the top two anomalies, not 30 metrics.
- Experiment idea: add a lightweight synthetic probe that mirrors typical 8‑token generation path to detect kernel regressions earlier.
- For Dedicated customers, include a separate cost delta threshold because reserved capacity changes the economics.
- Documented failures from last quarter: two false positives from conflated CDN errors; add CDN filter to alerting ruleset.
- Open questions: should QA own the quality-regression harness or Solutions Eng? leaning towards Solutions Eng for faster iteration.
